title: Compliance Director, Trust Company and Custody Operations
description: Vestwell is the financial technology company powering the new savings economy. The New York City-based fintech platform redefines how people save for the critical aspects of life across retirement, education, and healthcare savings needs. Today, Vestwell enables over 790,000 businesses and more than 2.75 million active savers, with over $57 billion in assets saved across all 50 United States.  Vestwell offers a range of products, including workplace-delivered retirement plans, employer-offered student loan repayment benefits, and various savings accounts for education, emergencies, and individuals with disabilities. Vestwell's platform serves a diverse clientele, including financial advisers, employers, third-party administrators, financial institutions, payroll providers, government agencies, and individual savers. To learn more, visit  vestwell.com Who Are We Looking For? We are seeking an experienced and strategic Compliance Director of Trust Company and Custody Operations to lead and manage regulatory compliance and operational oversight across our trust company, custodial, and trading operations. This individual will play a key role in ensuring compliance with all applicable regulations related to 401(k) plans, ERISA, and trust and custody services. The ideal candidate will bring a deep understanding of regulatory requirements, operational excellence, and a proven track record in managing regulatory operations within financial services or trust company and retirement plan administration. What Will You Be Doing? Lead the regulatory operations function with a focus on qualified retirement plans , particularly 401(k) plans, IRAs, and Emergency Savings Accounts. Create and implement procedures and internal controls for all trading activities within our custodial operations and proactively monitor our teams and systems for compliance with applicable laws and regulations.   Ensure compliance with ERISA , Internal Revenue Code (IRC) , DOL , IRS , trust company regulations, and SEC regulations. Oversee and enhance controls related to trust and custody operations, as well as state savings programs , ensuring alignment with fiduciary standards and regulatory expectations. Provide regular reporting to internal stakeholders and Risk Committee about material risks, incidents, and the effectiveness of risk mitigation strategies.  Partner with internal stakeholders (legal, compliance, product, operations) to interpret new and existing regulations and apply them to business practices. Monitor regulatory developments and proactively advise senior leadership on potential business impacts and required changes. Serve as the lead for  the Legal Team to lead the Vestwell Trust Company SOC 1 audit and New Hampshire Banking Department regulatory exam.  Liaise with external auditors, regulatory agencies, and third-party service providers during examinations, audits, inquiries, or other matters as needed.  Oversee and support regulatory reporting and filings (e.g., Form 5500, IRS/DOL disclosures). Manage a team of regulatory operations professionals, providing leadership, coaching, and performance oversight. Drive continuous improvement and automation of regulatory and compliance processes and controls. Requirements The Necessities Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field required; advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., JD, CPA, CRSP, QKA, CISP) preferred. Minimum of 10+ years of experience with a proven track record in regulatory compliance or operations in the retirement, trust, or custodial services industry. Deep knowledge of ERISA, 401(k) regulations, trust company laws, custody services, and applicable IRS/DOL regulations. Experience managing operational risk, compliance audits, and regulatory examinations. Strong leadership and team management skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across functions. Exceptional organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Experience working with recordkeeping platforms, trust accounting systems, or custodial platforms is a plus. The Extras Start up experience This role will be based in the New York City office, and will be part of Vestwell's hybrid in-office operation. The expected base salary range for this position is $160K - $180K base. This position is eligible to participate in the Company Bonus Pool and is eligible to receive new hire equity in the Company. Please note that salary bands are based on NY and other similar metro areas and may differ based on where the role is ultimately hired. At Vestwell, we prioritize employee wellbeing through comprehensive health benefits, generous time off, and a dedicated Employee Wellbeing Committee. title: Model Risk Manager
description: About the role: Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.  Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.  Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively. What you’ll do: Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk. Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality. Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD. Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact. Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues. Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose. Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use. Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution. Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals. Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees. Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates. Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient. Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition. Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk. What we’re looking for: 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development,  quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting. Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.  Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2. Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models. Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics. title: Senior Commissions Manager
description: Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence. This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk. Role Overview   As the Senior Commission Manager, you will serve as a key operational leader driving execution, calculation integrity, and continuous process optimization across Okta’s end-to-end sales compensation lifecycle. Supporting a high-growth field organization, this role bridges hands-on commission administration—validations, payment submissions, dispute resolution, and operational modernization—with advanced reporting, enterprise analytics, and AI-driven process automation. With a sharp focus on execution, data and incentive design governance, process engineering, and emerging AI tools, you will eliminate manual bottlenecks, build scalable reporting infrastructure, and guarantee 100% payout accuracy within tight deadlines. Key Responsibilities Commission Execution & Calculation Integrity Oversee the monthly commission calculation and payout lifecycle for global sellers, actively streamlining and operationalizing processes to maintain near-zero error margins. Operationalize data reconciliations between upstream source systems (CRM and Workday) and Xactly Incent, optimizing workflows to safeguard data integrity, maintain accurate crediting rules, and ensure calculation accuracy. Process Engineering, Automation & AI Map core commission workflows to eliminate friction, slash monthly close processing times, and eliminate manual data manipulation. Identify and deploy automation tools, custom scripts, AI-driven efficiencies to streamline commission validations, accruals, payment submissions, and reporting. Cross-Functional Partnership & Governance Drive alignment across GTM Strategy, Sales Operations, Finance, and IT on process improvement priorities and shared initiatives and/or projects. Lead change management for new tools, processes, and operating models — ensuring adoption is fast, smooth, and well-supported. Reporting & High-Impact Analytics Build and maintain scalable operational frameworks, seller performance dashboards, and executive reporting in BI tools (e.g., Tableau). Monitor payout-to-revenue ratios, quota attainment distributions, error rates, and operational SLA performance. Governance & SOX Compliance Maintain audit-ready control documentation and management review controls across the end-to-end commission processes.  Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external audit engagements. Team Leadership & Escalation Management Manage, mentor, and inspire a high-performing global commission operations team. Act as the primary escalation point for complex rep inquiry resolutions and payment adjustments. Desired Experience & Qualifications Core Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in sales compensation operations, incentive compensation management (ICM), or revenue operations, with a strong emphasis on execution, analytics, and system optimization. Scale & Precision: Proven success running commission processing for mid-to-large enterprise sales organizations (700+ reps) under tight close deadlines. Technical Stack Mastery: Deep hands-on experience with enterprise ICM platforms (e.g., Xactly), CRM platforms (Salesforce), SQL, BI tools (Tableau, Power BI), and advanced Excel proficiency. Cross-Functional Influence: Demonstrated success collaborating with GTM Strategy, Sales Operations, Accounting, FP&A, and Legal on exception workflows and financial compliance. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Systems, or equivalent practical experience.
